records.title: Dongwan Zhike granules attenuate OVA-induced airway inflammation by modulating IL-17 signaling and gut microbiota-EPA metabolic remodeling.
records.abstract: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease involving immune dysregulation and epithelial barrier impairment. Dongwan Zhike granules (DW), a multicomponent botanical formulation, exhibits potential anti-inflammatory effects, but its pharmacological mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the therapeutic effects and mechanisms of DW in allergic airway inflammation. The chemical composition of DW was characterized using a ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with Q Exactive mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q Exactive MS). An ovalbumin (OVA)-induced mouse model was established to evaluate airway inflammation. Integrated lung transcriptomics, gut microbiota sequencing, serum metabolomics, and an IL-17A-stimulated airway organoid model were applied to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. DW alleviated OVA-induced airway pathological injury and inflammatory cell infiltration. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that DW suppressed interleukin-17 (IL-17) signaling-related genes, including Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Mmp13, S100a8, and S100a9. Multiomics analysis revealed that DW treatment was associated with gut microbial remodeling and alterations in eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)-related lipid metabolism. In airway organoids, DW and EPA reduced IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α production and preserved ZO-1 expression, supporting EPA as a candidate metabolic mediator associated with the effects of DW. DW attenuates airway inflammation through modulation of IL-17-associated inflammatory responses, accompanied by alterations in gut microbial composition and EPA-related lipid metabolism. These findings provide preclinical evidence supporting further investigation of DW in allergic airway inflammation.

records.title: Human foetal cortical slice cultures: A translational platform for studying early neurodevelopment.
records.abstract: The developing human neocortex is characterised by complex and dynamic changes in cellular architecture, neuronal organisation and activity. We previously described how human foetal cortical organotypic slice cultures, prepared from ethically sourced tissue could be used to investigate these processes. Cultures can be maintained for weeks, exhibiting features of the normal developing brain that are not replicated in current organoid models. Such cultures allow the possibility for experimental manipulation, for instance testing the effects of genetic mutations. Here we extend the characterisation of our model. We report that these organotypic cultures preserve the laminar organisation of the developing cortical wall and show considerable diversity of neuronal morphology. Employing bulk mRNA hybridisation for 794 genes (a "human neuropathology" gene panel), we identified consistent patterns of evolving gene expression between 0 and 14 days in vitro (DIV) across different tissue samples taken at 16-18 post-conceptional weeks (pcw). To put this in the context of the normal developmental pattern, we compared our data set with previously acquired tissue RNAseq data collected between 7-17 pcw (https://www.hdbr.org/expression). This indicated that many gene expression changes in vitro followed prior developmental trajectories, but others diverged strongly, including upregulated genes associated with responses to stress, and downregulated genes associated with the vascular function. This latter effect may reflect the redundancy of vascular development in culture. Notably, various genes associated with pre- and post- synaptic function, including both glutamate and GABA receptors, continued to be expressed strongly. Consistent with this, we observed spontaneous neuronal network activity in the subplate (SP) using targeted expression of the genetically encoded Ca2+ indicator, GCaMPf6, to post-mitotic neurons. The frequency of neuronal Ca2+ transients increased when blockers of either GABAA receptors or gap junctions were applied. Conversely, activity was significantly reduced by glutamatergic receptor antagonists and abolished by voltage gated sodium channel blockade. Neuronal Ca2+ transients were triggered directly by focal application of glutamate in the SP and subventricular zone, whereas cortical plate neurons exhibited weaker responses. This was consistent with levels of immunoreactivity for glutamate receptor sub-units in these compartments. In conclusion, the organotypic cultures show functional synaptic networks, supported by continued expression of the relevant synaptic protein machinery. These data provide further validation of organotypic cultures as a model for investigating and manipulating the early prenatal development of human neocortex, a period that is otherwise difficult to study.

records.title: Emerging Brain Tumor Organoid Models for Studying Tumor Heterogeneity, Microenvironmental Interactions, and Therapeutic Response.
records.abstract: Brain tumors are genetically and cellularly heterogeneous and interact extensively with neural, vascular, immune, and extracellular microenvironments that conventional experimental models reproduce incompletely. This review examines how brain tumor organoids are generated, how they have been applied in brain tumor research, and the challenges that must be overcome for broader application. Current approaches differ along two largely independent axes: whether tumor cells are derived directly from patient tissue or generated through defined genetic alterations, and whether the surrounding microenvironment is retained from the source tissue or deliberately reconstructed. We discuss how these models have been used to study genetic drivers of tumor initiation, intratumoral heterogeneity, tumor-microenvironment interactions, mechanisms of invasion, and patient-specific therapeutic responses and resistance. Across these applications, organoids have provided experimentally tractable systems in which to investigate tumor cell-state plasticity, tumor-neural interactions, microenvironmental regulation of tumor behavior, and variability in treatment response while preserving features of human disease often lost in conventional systems. At the same time, model establishment remains variable, cultures can diverge during prolonged propagation, and vascular and immune compartments remain incompletely represented. Brain tumor organoids therefore complement rather than replace two-dimensional culture systems, genetically engineered mouse models, and patient-derived xenografts. Future progress will depend on rigorous standardization of organoid generation and characterization, together with the selective incorporation of biological and engineering complexity according to the specific experimental or therapeutic question being addressed.

records.title: Phytochemical Profiling of the Halophyte Suaeda vera and Antileishmanial Evaluation of Its Extracts and Selected Metabolites, with In Silico ADMET Analysis.
records.abstract: Plant-derived secondary metabolites are a promising source of new anti-infective agents owing to their remarkable chemical diversity and broad spectrum of biological activities. Among them, halophytes are particularly promising because adaptation to saline environments promotes the accumulation of structurally diverse secondary metabolites. In the present study, organic extracts from four Tunisian halophytic species collected across different seasons were evaluated for their activity against Leishmania infantum axenic amastigotes, the etiological agent of visceral leishmaniasis in the Mediterranean Basin. Among the species tested, Suaeda vera was the only one to exhibit significant antileishmanial activity. Mass spectrometry-based phytochemical profiling of the bioactive extracts resulted in the putative annotation of 53 secondary metabolites and revealed qualitative differences in their annotated chemical composition among the seasonal samples. Three compounds putatively annotated in the active extracts-demethylzeylasteral, caffeic acid, and protocatechuic aldehyde-were subsequently evaluated individually using commercially available reference compounds and exhibited EC50 values of 0.20, 1.09, and 14.56 μM, respectively. Caffeic acid displayed the most favorable overall profile, combining potent antileishmanial activity with a high selectivity index (SI > 91.7) in mouse intestinal organoids. In vitro assays revealed that none of the three compounds inhibited trypanothione reductase-associated activity. Furthermore, in silico drug-likeness and ADMET analyses suggested that caffeic acid may have a comparatively favorable predicted pharmacokinetic and toxicity profile among the three compounds evaluated. Collectively, these findings highlight S. vera as a promising source of antileishmanial metabolites and establish caffeic acid as the most promising hit compound for further investigation.

records.title: Bile Acid Stress Disrupts Homeostasis and Placental Functional Programs in Human First-Trimester Trophoblast Organoids.
records.abstract: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is characterized by elevated maternal bile acids (BAs), yet their effects on human trophoblast organization and transcriptional responses remain incompletely understood. Here, we used human first-trimester trophoblast organoids (TOs) to characterize cellular and transcriptional responses to a defined six-component BA mixture (50-150 μM). BA exposure disrupted organoid architecture and intercellular organization, with attenuated proliferation-associated features and more prominent SDC1 staining. These changes were accompanied by increased DNA fragmentation and cleaved caspase-3 staining and by reduced ATP-dependent viability, supporting an apoptotic component of BA-associated trophoblast injury. Bulk RNA sequencing after exposure to 150 μM BA for 96 h identified 413 differentially expressed genes, of which 364 were downregulated and 49 were upregulated. Downregulated transcripts were primarily associated with placental endocrine and secretory processes, epithelial organization, cell adhesion, and transport, whereas a smaller subset of lipid-handling genes was upregulated. RT-qPCR confirmed concordant upregulation of PLIN2 and ABCG1 in two independent donor-derived TO lines. Collectively, these findings show that BA mixture exposure is associated with structural injury and altered transcriptional profiles in human TOs, thereby providing insight into trophoblast responses to BA stress.

records.title: Construction and Application of Testicular Organoid Models in Multi-Omics-Driven Male Reproductive Toxicity Assessment: A Review.
records.abstract: Conventional male reproductive toxicity testing relies on rodent bioassays and two-dimensional cultures, which are limited by species extrapolation, low throughput, and weak mechanistic resolution. Testicular and seminiferous-tubule organoids partially restore the Sertoli-Leydig-peritubular myoid niche and permit serial, non-terminal sampling, making them compatible with multi-omics profiling in a way earlier models were not. This review examines the field across four layers: the biological hierarchy and regulatory pathways that constrain model design; organoid construction strategies together with computational simulation of morphogenesis and mass transport; multi-omics integration algorithms and toxicity feature extraction; and retrospective validation on publicly deposited datasets. We compare cell sourcing, scaffold, and culture configuration routes against tubule formation and meiotic completion, derive critical-radius and shear-stress criteria governing construct viability, and evaluate similarity network fusion, latent factor decomposition, joint matrix factorization, and graph neural network approaches. Retrospective modeling indicates that adding epigenomic input to transcriptomic features yields the largest performance gain, that gradient-boosted trees outperform deep networks at current sample sizes, and that attribution profiles align with established mechanisms. We contribute an integration framework dimensioned for testicular organoid data, a fully open-source reproducible pipeline, and an explicit mapping between quantitative organoid descriptors and toxicity endpoints. Persistent obstacles include incomplete structural reconstitution biasing omics signal, sparse and inconsistently annotated public data, simulation parameter uncertainty, and unverified cross-species transfer. Minimum reporting standards, a shared characterization vocabulary, and an open benchmark platform are proposed as prerequisites for regulatory uptake.

records.title: FeDx-SF@βE assembly for AML treatment via GATA1/SLC40A1 pathway-mediated iron homeostasis disorder.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. Inducing ferroptosis in AML cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, transcriptomic analyses first revealed that ferroptosis-associated transcriptional states were closely associated with prognosis and ex vivo drug-response heterogeneity in AML, providing a rationale for ferroptosis-oriented therapeutic design. Based on these findings, and further supported by a transcriptome-based target-scoring strategy, β-elemene (βE), a clinically used natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, was selected as a candidate ferroptosis-related agent. We subsequently developed a nanodelivery system, designated FeDx-SF@βE, based on alcohol-induced silk fibroin (SF) folding to co-deliver ferric dextran (FeDx) and βE. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited a uniform particle size of 182.3 nm, favorable colloidal stability, and sustained drug release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of FeDx-SF@βE by AML cells, leading to significantly inhibited cell viability. Pharmacological cell-death inhibitor rescue experiments showed that ferrostatin-1 produced the most pronounced protective effect, indicating that FeDx-SF@βE-induced AML cell death was predominantly ferroptosis-dependent. Mechanistically, βE-containing treatment suppressed the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor GATA1 and downregulated the iron efflux channel SLC40A1. GATA1/SLC40A1 gain- and loss-of-function analyses further demonstrated that activation of this axis attenuated FeDx-SF@βE-induced iron overload and ferroptotic injury, whereas suppression of this axis promoted intracellular iron retention, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. In combination with FeDx-derived iron supply, βE-mediated inhibition of the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-export axis resulted in intracellular iron overload, glutathione depletion, ROS accumulation, extensive lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Bulk transcriptomic and virtual-cell analyses further supported the involvement of the GATA1/SLC40A1 axis in ferroptosis-associated AML states and linked βE-related transcriptional programs to this regulatory mechanism. In a disseminated AML xenograft model, FeDx-SF@βE exhibited enhanced antileukemic efficacy and favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work provides a combined ferroptosis-oriented nanotherapeutic strategy for AML treatment and highlights the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-homeostasis axis as a functionally relevant mechanism for ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicine design.

records.title: scREFINE: Label-efficient refinement of frozen scGPT embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq clustering.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) clustering remains challenging because of high dimensionality, sparsity, technical noise, and limited cell annotations. Here, we propose scREFINE, a label-efficient semi-supervised clustering framework that adapts pretrained single-cell foundation-model embeddings for accurate cell clustering. scREFINE uses a lightweight refinement head to map cells into a task-specific clustering space using only 5% labeled cells, while treating the remaining cells as unlabeled during training. To exploit information from unlabeled cells, scREFINE introduces stability-aware soft structural regularization over local neighborhoods, which leverages reliable cell-cell relations as auxiliary guidance without relying on hard pseudo-label constraints. Experiments on five benchmark scRNA-seq datasets show that scREFINE achieves the best ARI on every dataset against every baseline under an identical, leakage-free protocol (mean ± SD over four seeds). A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test over the five per-dataset means yields p=0.0625, above the conventional 0.05 threshold because only five datasets are available; we therefore interpret the consistent improvements as strong empirical evidence rather than a statistically conclusive demonstration. A common-embedding comparison confirms that these gains arise from task-specific refinement rather than the pretrained representation alone: adapted baselines receiving identical embeddings achieve 0.00-0.61 ARI, compared with 0.73-0.89 for scREFINE. Ablation analyses further demonstrate that task-specific embedding refinement is the primary driver of improvement, whereas soft structural regularization provides dataset-dependent auxiliary gains and degrades more gracefully than hard pseudo-labels when supervision is scarce. Biological marker-gene analysis confirms that the predicted clusters correspond to canonical cell populations.

records.title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network.
records.abstract: Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean R2 of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: MultiFlow: coupled flow matching for predicting single-cell multiomic perturbation responses in unseen cellular contexts.
records.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation requires resolving coordinated changes across molecular layers, yet most single-cell perturbation models focus on transcriptional responses alone. Here we present MultiFlow, a coupled flow-matching framework that unifies generation and perturbation prediction of paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Through bidirectional information exchange between RNA and ATAC generative flows, MultiFlow learns how their joint distribution depends on cellular context and perturbation identity. Across multiomic generation benchmarks, MultiFlow accurately reproduced paired RNA-ATAC states and their population distributions. In multiome perturbation benchmarks, MultiFlow achieved the strongest overall performance in predicting both gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility perturbation responses, outperforming modality-specific perturbation-prediction methods in cell types whose perturbed states were withheld from training. Joint multiomic modeling further preserved perturbation-induced coordination between modalities, including concordant peak-gene effects and cross-modal cellular neighborhood structure. These results establish MultiFlow as a unified generative framework for modeling paired molecular states and predicting their coordinated perturbation responses across cellular contexts. Code and tutorial of MultiFlow are available at https://github.com/liuq-lab/MultiFlow.

records.title: Prediction transfer does not imply reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models.
records.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are increasingly transferred across tissues, diseases, perturbation screens, and experimental platforms. Although substantial effort has focused on prediction transfer, it remains unclear whether a model's assessment of its own reliability transfers similarly across biological contexts. Here we define reliability transfer as the ability to transfer an accurate assessment of when model predictions are likely to be correct or incorrect and investigate its behavior across ten perturbation-prediction systems spanning multiple datasets, models, and evaluation settings. We find that reliability transfer varies substantially across source-target pairs and cannot be inferred from predictive performance alone, indicating that prediction transfer and reliability transfer constitute distinct forms of generalization. Analyses of biological annotations, network connectivity, target exposure, and contextual factors reveal that prediction reliability is associated with both shared and context-dependent signals, with their relative importance differing across systems. To characterize this variability, we introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints, context-level signatures derived from strictly cross-fitted SHAP explanations that summarize how reliability estimators combine biological and contextual information when assigning confidence. Across systems, contexts with similar attribution-magnitude fingerprints tended to transfer reliability more successfully, and fingerprint similarity identified transfer sources achieving higher reliability-transfer performance within the observed candidate set. However, these relationships weakened under stricter cross-family transfer settings, indicating that transferable reliability structure remains partly dependent on shared contextual information. Finally, transferred reliability estimators produced different perturbation rankings despite identical perturbation predictions, illustrating a practical consequence of reliability transfer for downstream prioritization. Together, these results establish reliability transfer as a distinct aspect of foundation-model generalization and introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints as a framework for characterizing transferable reliability structure across biological contexts.

records.title: Tuned Fitness Landscapes for Benchmarking Model-Guided Protein Design.
records.abstract: Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involves many design choices across the design-build-test-learn loop ranging from data collection strategies to modeling. The cost of collecting experimental data makes benchmarking every component of these pipelines prohibitively difficult, necessitating the development of synthetic landscapes. In this work, we develop a framework called SLIP ("Synthetic Landscape Inference for Proteins") for constructing synthetic landscapes with tunable difficulty based on Potts models. This framework can be extended to any protein family for which there is a sequence alignment. We show that our tuning framework provides landscapes sufficiently challenging to benchmark MLDE pipelines. SLIP is open-source and is available at https://github.com/google-research/slip.

records.title: AI-Assisted Molecular Structure Prediction from Tandem Mass Spectra: Reliability and Validation.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has broadened the interpretation of tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) beyond experimental library matching, enabling molecular fingerprint prediction, candidate ranking, and generation of previously unlisted structures. Yet these outputs do not all support the same claim about chemical identity. This review briefly summarizes database-restricted retrieval, database-free generation, and scaffold-guided hybrid methods, and then asks what additional evidence is needed to turn a plausible structure into a defensible annotation. We examine failure modes involving incomplete candidate spaces, erroneous precursor assignments, structurally related isomers, leakage between training and test data, and misinterpreted confidence scores. The review contributes two practical elements: a candidate-discrimination workflow, in which alternative structures are retained and targeted measurements such as multienergy fragmentation, retention behavior, ion mobility, and authentic standards are selected according to the unresolved structural question; and an evidence-to-claim checklist that links each question to the most informative measurement and to the strongest supportable identification confidence level. Both synthesize established analytical principles for small-molecule electrospray LC-HRMS/MS rather than constituting a validated scoring algorithm. By making the basis of each annotation transparent, they are intended to improve the practical value of AI-assisted MS/MS in metabolomics, pharmaceutical analysis, environmental screening, and forensic toxicology.

records.title: Emerging Computational Advances in Simulating PCSK9 Variant Dynamics for Therapeutic Design Against Hypercholesterolemia.
records.abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a premier model for precision medicine, having moved from genetic discovery to approved therapeutics within two decades. Yet despite the clinical success of monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNA and the newly approved oral macrocyclic-peptide inhibitor class, targeting PCSK9 remains a demanding biophysical challenge. Clinical translation has concentrated almost entirely on the rigid, well-resolved subtilisin-like catalytic domain that interfaces with the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR). By contrast, the C-terminal cysteine- and histidine-rich domain (CHRD), which governs allosteric regulation, protein trafficking and post-translational modification, is highly disordered and largely elusive in experimental structures, leaving a critical regulatory network therapeutically unexploited. This review examines how advanced computational biology is bridging that structural gap, organizing the computational landscape of PCSK9 around the biophysical mechanisms of gain- and loss-of-function variants. We detail how explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, free-energy calculations and cryptic-pocket detection expose the functional plasticity and allosteric networks that static crystallography cannot capture, and we evaluate the convergence of these physics-based approaches with artificial intelligence, including deep-learning structure prediction and generative design of de novo nanobody and peptide binders. Therapeutic development and the structural literature currently point in diverging directions: drug discovery remains focused on the crowded LDLR-binding interface, whereas computational methods are beginning to identify candidate sites beyond it. We argue that the next advance in PCSK9 therapeutics will come from integrating generative artificial intelligence with rigorous enhanced sampling in a unified pipeline, deliberately shifting focus toward the disordered regulatory domains that have evaded classical screening.

records.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function.
records.abstract: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs. First, we present a generative method that combines nonlinear per-domain sequence-to-score landscapes with connectivity-dependent synthetic readouts. Second, we propose a graph neural network architecture that explicitly encodes these topological constraints, distinguishing between format configurations that appear identical to the evaluated connectivity-agnostic multilayer perceptron. We demonstrate that this model learns topology-dependent structure-function relationships on synthetic landscapes and evaluate a transfer learning workflow as infrastructure for adaptation to biological datasets. We showcase our framework with a trispecific T cell engager-inspired synthetic topology-dependent optimization task and a constrained ranking of common light chain candidates against a composite objective. This work provides a controlled benchmarking environment for developing and evaluating topology-aware computational tools for msAb modeling. All experiments use synthetic data; no biological validation is performed.

records.title: Protein engineering in Brazil: a biophysical perspective.
records.abstract: Protein engineering has become an increasingly interdisciplinary field, integrating molecular biology, structural biology, biophysics, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence to modify protein structure, stability, dynamics, molecular recognition, and catalytic activity. This systematic review examines the historical development and scientific contributions of protein engineering research associated with Brazilian institutions between 1988 and June 2026. A total of 792 peer-reviewed articles were identified in PubMed through eight thematic search strategies covering protein and enzyme engineering, directed evolution, rational and computational design, recombinant protein expression, therapeutic proteins, structural biology, and artificial intelligence-assisted engineering. The reviewed literature reveals a transition from early residue-level mutagenesis and conventional biochemical assays to increasingly integrated experimental and computational approaches. Advances in X-ray crystallography, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), circular dichroism (CD), mass spectrometry, small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), calorimetry, molecular dynamics, and structural bioinformatics enabled the quantitative investigation of protein folding, stability, conformational landscapes, molecular interactions, and catalytic mechanisms. More recently, machine learning, protein language models, AlphaFold-derived structures, and generative approaches have expanded the capacity to predict mutations and design proteins, peptides, antibodies, and enzymes with predefined properties. Overall, protein engineering in Brazil has evolved into a mature and diverse field with applications in health, infectious diseases, agriculture, biotechnology, bioenergy, biomaterials, environmental remediation, and industrial biocatalysis. The findings indicate that biophysics has moved beyond a predominantly descriptive role and has become central to the design and validation of engineered proteins. Future progress will depend on the convergence of experimental biophysics, multiscale simulations, artificial intelligence, high-throughput validation, and stronger national and international research networks.

records.title: Evolutionary divergence of uric acid catabolic enzymes: structure-function constraints and genomic innovations across taxa.
records.abstract: Uric acid degradation is a model for understanding how gene duplication, loss, and functional divergence drive metabolic evolution. In hominoids and uricotelic animals, uric acid is the terminal purine catabolite, whereas most other taxa further degrade it to allantoin and beyond. Comparative genomics and structural analyses reveal recurrent duplication and repurposing of key enzymes. 5-Hydroxyisourate hydrolase (HIUase) and transthyretin (TTR) share a common ancestral hydrolase, later diverging through neofunctionalization, while independent gene fusions reshaped the pathway, notably the gene fusion of Urah (HIUase) and Urad (2-oxo-4-hydroxy-4-carboxy-5-ureidoimidazoline decarboxylase, or OHCUd) into single-chain allantoin synthases in plants, diatoms, and bacteria. Elastic network modeling this gene fusion shows uncorrelated motions between the catalytic domains, suggesting its advantage stems from fixed stoichiometry and spatial proximity rather than conformational coupling. Further divergence is seen in enzyme families with complementary substrate specificities, and gene clustering in bacteria and yeast reflects regulatory optimization under nitrogen limitation, paralleling the ureide pathway in legumes. In hominoids, pseudogenization of urate oxidase relaxed constraints on downstream enzymes, elevating serum uric acid, an ancestral adaptation now linked to hyperuricemia. Gut microbiome-mediated degradation and links between Urad variants and cancer risk underscore the pathway's continuing relevance. Mammalian Urad orthologs show strong sequence conservation. Molecular modeling of the human ortholog demonstrated a conserved fold, consistent with a predominantly α-helical secondary structure content supported by circular dichroism, whereas kinetic characterization revealed the absence of detectable catalytic activity. Building on these principles, evolution-guided protein engineering achieved partial functional interconversion between transthyretins and HIUases without disrupting the ancestral scaffold, revealing purine catabolism's plasticity as a model for enzyme innovation and the metabolism-disease-protein design interface.

records.title: Sequencing-informed, patient-specific droplet digital PCR assays for circulating tumor DNA monitoring in recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer: a pilot study.
records.abstract: In recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC), early identification of treatment response remains challenging because imaging may be delayed or confounded by treatment-related changes and atypical response patterns under immunotherapy. Serial circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis may provide a minimally invasive measure of tumor dynamics and complement conventional imaging. We therefore investigated the feasibility and clinical relevance of patient-specific droplet digital PCR (ddPCR)-based ctDNA monitoring. Nine patients with R/M HNSCC underwent tumor genomic profiling using FoundationOne® CDx as part of routine clinical care. Patient-specific single-nucleotide variants, including pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and technically suitable variants of uncertain significance, were selected for ddPCR assay development. Plasma samples were collected before and/or during systemic treatment, and ctDNA kinetics were assessed in relation to radiologic response, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). Sixteen single-target ddPCR assays were successfully established and combined into ten patient-specific single- or multi-target assay configurations. A total of 21 plasma samples were analyzed, and technically valid measurements were obtained for all samples. Pretreatment plasma was available for seven patients, of whom three (42.9%) had detectable ctDNA. Across all time points, ctDNA was detected at least once in six of nine patients (66.7%). Among the six patients with serial sampling, ctDNA kinetics showed descriptive agreement with radiologic assessment in five (83.3%). The single patient with increasing ctDNA developed progressive disease, whereas decreasing or stable ctDNA was accompanied by partial response or stable disease in four patients; one patient showed a mixed radiologic response. In an exploratory descriptive comparison, the single patient with increasing ctDNA had shorter observed PFS and OS than the five patients with decreasing or stable ctDNA levels. Given the group size of one patient, this observation is hypothesis-generating and does not establish a prognostic association. Patient-specific ddPCR-based ctDNA monitoring was technically feasible and showed agreement with radiologic assessment in most evaluable patients. These proof-of-concept findings support prospective evaluation of patient-specific ddPCR as a focused approach for longitudinal monitoring in R/M HNSCC; its comparative clinical utility and cost-effectiveness remain to be established.

records.title: High Time for Pathology AI: Practical Considerations for Turning Potential into Practice.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, and efficiency in anatomical pathology, but technical success alone does not establish clinical utility. In this Perspective, we examine practical requirements for translating computational pathology tools into routine practice, including prioritization of genuine clinical bottlenecks, representative datasets, independent validation, workflow integration, costs, clinician oversight, regulatory compliance, and post-deployment monitoring. We distinguish evidence from retrospective model evaluations, controlled reader studies, prospective workflow assessments, and economic simulations, recognizing that their conclusions are not interchangeable. We also propose a staged, decision-oriented framework through which laboratories can assess clinical need, select technologies, perform local validation, conduct prospective pilots, deploy with safeguards, and monitor performance throughout the AI lifecycle. Evidence from selected applications is encouraging, but effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and readiness for routine use vary by intended purpose and practice environment. Responsible adoption should therefore be guided by demonstrated clinical benefit, operational feasibility, and ongoing evaluation rather than algorithmic performance alone.

records.title: Circulating Non-Coding RNAs as Liquid Biopsy Biomarkers for Early Detection of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer: From Diagnostic Performance to Clinical Translation.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive and molecularly heterogeneous breast cancer subtype for which early detection remains clinically important. Circulating non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs), are being investigated as blood-based biomarkers. This narrative review evaluates the clinical evidence for circulating ncRNAs as liquid-biopsy biomarkers for early TNBC detection, focusing on stage I-II disease, diagnostic performance, comparator selection, and validation. Methods: Peer-reviewed studies published between 2009 and October 2026 were identified primarily through PubMed/MEDLINE searches, supplemented by Google Scholar searches, with particular attention to disease stage, comparator populations, diagnostic performance, and validation status. Results: Among the ncRNA classes reviewed, circulating miRNAs provide the most directly relevant, although still limited, clinical evidence for early-stage TNBC detection, whereas evidence for lncRNAs and circRNAs remains predominantly exploratory and insufficiently validated for early-stage detection. Translation is limited by small, heterogeneous cohorts, analytical variability, and insufficient independent and prospective validation. Conclusions: High diagnostic accuracy in selected cohorts does not establish clinical readiness. Standardized analytical workflows, independent multicenter validation, prospective evaluation in intended-use populations, and integration with imaging and clinical assessment are needed before circulating ncRNA signatures can be considered for clinical use.

records.title: Immune-Related Proteomic Profiling in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: Tissue and Soluble Biofluid Biomarkers.
records.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) shows complex interactions with the tumor microenvironment, involving a range of immune checkpoint proteins and circulating biomarkers that may influence disease progression and response to treatment. Recent technological advances have identified tissue-based and circulating immune-related proteomic targets such as programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4), and circulating interleukin-8 (cIL-8) as potential diagnostic, prognostic and predictive biomarkers. Despite significant progress, ccRCC remains a major clinical challenge due to its diverse molecular and immunological characteristics that hinder the clinical utility of these biomarkers. The present review provides an updated overview of the current evidence regarding immune-related proteomic biomarkers in ccRCC, including both tissue-derived and circulating proteins. Herein, we discuss the potential diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive value of such agents, emphasizing their biological significance and potential to guide personalized immunotherapeutic strategies. Particular attention is given to the developing liquid-biopsy-based techniques and their application as novel minimally invasive methods of identifying new targets for disease monitoring and treatment evaluation. Finally, we focus on emerging therapeutic approaches and combined strategies, highlighting how biomarker-driven precision oncology continues to reshape ccRCC management.

records.title: Folate Receptor Alpha (FRα/FOLR1) in Cancer: Diagnostic, Prognostic or Predictive Biomarker? A Critical Review of Its Clinical Utility.
records.abstract: Folate receptor alpha (FRα) plays a key role in folate homeostasis. Folate is involved, among other processes, in nucleotide biosynthesis, and the marked difference between FRα expression in certain cancers and under physiological conditions gives this receptor potential as a cancer biomarker. However, the current state of knowledge points to a specific role for this marker and defines its potential place in cancer diagnosis and treatment. This review aims to critically evaluate the available evidence regarding the clinical utility of FRα. Analysis of the literature indicates that despite differences in expression, the sensitivity and specificity of FRα are insufficient for its use as a standalone diagnostic marker. In contrast, its potential as a prognostic marker is strongly dependent on cancer type. The strongest evidence of clinical utility concerns membranous FRα protein expression assessed by a validated immunohistochemical companion diagnostic assay for selecting patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer for mirvetuximab soravtansine treatment. In contrast, the predictive relevance of FRα for other targeted therapeutic strategies remains under investigation. Overall, FRα should be regarded as a clinically actionable biomarker in a defined therapeutic setting and as a promising, but not universally validated, diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive candidate in other oncological applications.

records.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Therapeutic Resistance in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health burden, and therapeutic resistance continues to limit the benefit from systemic treatment. Despite advances in systemic therapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitor-based combinations, antiangiogenic agents, and multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors for patients with advanced HCC, primary non-response and acquired resistance are common. This review summarizes the mechanisms that underlie resistance to contemporary HCC therapies, including tumour heterogeneity, molecular pathway rewiring and crosstalk, tumour microenvironment and immune escape, epigenetic alterations, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and cancer stem cell expansion. We discuss how these mechanisms limit the efficacy of current doublet and triplet regimens, and why biologically rational combinations do not consistently translate into clinical benefit. Emerging strategies to overcome resistance, including biomarker-enriched trial designs and liquid biopsy are also discussed. A deeper integration of mechanistic insights with translational biomarkers will be essential to improve treatment durability and clinical outcomes for patients with HCC.
